findings.summary: Duplicates the capability owned by scripts/prototypes/compile_pass_profile/profile.py: the same control(), build(), checkpoint() sequence, the same receipt fields and the same cache_guard ledger, re-emitted as a copy rather than a parameterised variant of the owner. The only new behaviour is the --block stub hook and the --expect-device refusal, both of which fit the owner as arguments, so a fix to the cold-process or receipt logic now has two sites. The node's fence excluded compile_pass_profile/, so the extension could not be made from this node.

Duplicates the lowering-only measurement owned by scripts/prototypes/compile_pass_profile/lowered_size.py: the same configure_dtypes/cache-off preamble, the same make_jaxpr then lower steps and the same two receipt fields, re-emitted with a block patch. The capability owner is lowered_size.py, which would take the --block hook as an argument; the copy means a change to the lowering measurement is now maintained in two files.

The receipt is written twice with no read or checkpoint between, so line 83's write is discarded by line 87's; only the second carries the 'reached' probe list. Harmless to the result but dead work in a script whose purpose is a durable receipt, and a reader cannot tell which write is authoritative.

The delivered manifest records neither baseline_suite nor after_suite nor test_logs, although the run executed a base and head arm (2 passed, 2 skipped in each). The only copies of those gate logs are under ~/.cache/nova-kernel-compile-barrier/point-program-attribution/suite/, so a coordinator reading the record alone cannot see that the pair ran or anything about it; the checkpoint line is the sole pointer.
